scope: Independent read-only design and prior-result review; no engine execution or build performed by this reviewer.

base_verification.decision: Keep common e3336e8 foundation and apply only PR64 diff there. The PR base SHA is older than the actual branch tip; it is not a newly changed upstream implementation.

valid_evidence: Whole native-process wall time and peak process commit are reported separately from instrumented attribution runs.
Invalid raw-dictionary transient outputs are excluded from performance claims.
Same-base double and dictionary comparisons avoid unrelated merged source-selection/residual changes.
Prior native cases use realistic particle rates and increase grid/group/height/source load.
Reported source-group count and external label limits distinguish actual reader restrictions from dictionary key support.
remaining_decision_gaps: Previous output-scan and closure-allocation explanations were profiling hypotheses; test each change independently before causal performance claims.
The 99-group, nine-height sparse case alone cannot justify a global default or automatic threshold.
Three measured runs establish large consistent effects but not stable tiny percentage improvements; repeat only close or noisy cases.
Store process commit, working set and GC allocated bytes as separate quantities. Do not infer retained heap or dictionary-entry overhead from peak commit alone.
No absolute deterministic guarantee follows from double accumulation; retain measured transient equality/error figures.
A reduced writer scan can affect output cache lifetime; test successive writes and formats explicitly.

first_stage.reason: Separate repeated full-output scans from update allocation/contention on two dominant adverse cases.

cases: same spatial/group layout as sparse99 with one output height
second_stage.purpose: Check worker scaling, output-height dependence and residual contribution preservation.

focused_checks: Reuse the actual compiled-DLL 84-output checks for new variants; retain -1, -2, -3 headers, centre/upper/lower masks, external SG labels and internal indices.
Exercise two successive writer cycles with changed dictionary keys/values to detect stale cached group/slice indexing.
Check output index construction/release does not alter central, upper or lower dictionaries or building-volume correction order.
For static AddOrUpdate callbacks, verify retry factories remain side-effect-free and each mass-times-dt addition uses the original double operation order.
If combination changes one-worker transient outputs, investigate before timing or publication.

recommendation_rules: Recommend the simple double array if dictionary follow-ups retain substantial cost across ordinary grids without offsetting memory benefit.
Recommend a corrected sparse implementation for memory-heavy grids if output indexing removes most large-case overhead while maintaining result preservation.
Prefer staged maintainer review of fixes and independent optimizations over a speculative automatic selector: thresholds require broader retained-memory and occupancy evidence.
Ask the maintainer whether to retain the array default plus optional sparse storage, or first refine the sparse branch further; indicate willingness to follow the preferred direction.
Mention source-group expansion as a separate small reader/ID change only; do not imply the dictionary alone removes existing limits.
comment_outline: Thank the developer and answer the proposed approach directly.
Give two representative timing/memory results and the tested workload range.
State newly demonstrated independent optimization effects using measured values.
Mention the reproduced residual/odour fixes briefly and link patch/evidence.
Recommend a concrete implementation path with one reasonable alternative and ask which is preferred.
